source_text:
78 Οὐ μόνον περὶ πόρνης εἴρηται, ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ πονηρᾶς ἐπιθυμίας· ὅταν γὰρ
ὁ νοῦς πρὸς τὴν κακὴν πρᾶξιν ὁρμήσῃ, τότε ἡ καρδία ὃ λέγει στόμα μελετᾷ σκολιά· τότε γὰρ ἔσται ὡς ἐν καρδίᾳ θαλάσσης, ὑπὸ τῆς ἅλμης τῶν πολλῶν λογισμῶν
thought_title: Evil desire as prostitute drowning the mind
orientation: Eustathius continues his commentary by explaining that the prostitute in Proverbs signifies evil desire, which overwhelms the mind like a pilot in a storm and drives it toward wicked action.
pass_a_gloss: Not only about prostitute [it] has-been-said but also about evil desire; for when the mind toward the bad action may-rush then the heart what [it] says mouth practices crooked [things]; for then [it] will-be as in heart of-sea by the brine of the many thoughts

choices.why: Glossary term πορνη = prostitute; Eustathius interprets the Proverbs figure as evil desire.
Glossary term πονηρὰ ἐπιθυμία = evil desire; the passage explicitly links the prostitute to this.
ὁρμάω with πρὸς indicates the mind directing its impulse toward an action; not merely 'rushes'.

choices.english: the heart meditates the crooked things which the mouth speaks
choices.why: The relative clause ὃ λέγει στόμα modifies σκολιά; the heart meditates what the mouth speaks, not a separate statement.
rejected: the heart meditates crooked things, and the mouth speaks them

choices.english: as in the heart of the sea
choices.why: No noun for 'ship' appears; the comparison is the mind's state to being in the sea's heart.
rejected: like a ship in the heart of the sea

choices.why: ἅλμη means surge or salt water; here the overwhelming flood of reasonings.

bible_refs.note: Passage on the prostitute / strange woman, which Eustathius interprets as evil desire.

pass_b_english: Not only has it been said concerning a prostitute, but also concerning evil desire. For when the mind sets itself toward wicked action, then the heart meditates the crooked things which the mouth speaks. For then the mind will be as in the heart of the sea, by the brine of its many thoughts.
notes: Source text ends mid-sentence at λογισμῶν; the following clause (πνιγόμενος … ἀγωνιᾷ) is in the next section.

problems.quote: For then it will be as in the heart of the sea, by the surge of the many thoughts.
problems.source_quote: τότε γὰρ ἔσται ὡς ἐν καρδίᾳ θαλάσσης, ὑπὸ τῆς ἅλμης τῶν πολλῶν λογισμῶν
problems.why: Subject 'it' is unclear (the mind); 'by the surge' lacks connection, and the pilot image from Prov 23.34 is implicit. Reader cannot follow.
problems.fix: For then the mind will be as in the heart of the sea, tossed by the brine of its many thoughts.

edits.old: For then it will be as in the heart of the sea, by the surge of the many thoughts.
edits.new: For then the mind will be as in the heart of the sea, tossed by the surge of its many thoughts.

fixed: Changed 'it' to 'the mind' to clarify the subject (Greek ἔσται with subject νοῦς from context); changed 'by the surge' to 'tossed by the surge' and added 'its' to link the thoughts to the mind, incorporating the implicit pilot/sea imagery from Prov 23:34 LXX.

problems.quote: tossed by the surge of its many thoughts
problems.source_quote: ὑπὸ τῆς ἅλμης τῶν πολλῶν λογισμῶν
problems.why: ἅλμη means brine/salt spray, not surge; also the source subject is the heart/mind as sea, so 'tossed' adds a verb the source lacks (text is truncated).
problems.fix: by the brine of its many thoughts

edits.old: tossed by the surge of its many thoughts
edits.new: by the brine of its many thoughts

fixed: Fixed mistranslation: 'surge' -> 'brine' for ἅλμη (brine/salt spray), and removed added verb 'tossed' which is not in the truncated source text. Source: ὑπὸ τῆς ἅλμης τῶν πολλῶν λογισμῶν.
